pagedata.pyUsage:
1. Obtain or compile an HTML stream that represents the content for a PDF document, or obtain the name of an HTML Stream rule that shares the applies-to class of the work page.
2. If possible, inject references to required CSS documents into the "head" element of the HTML stream (this is a REQUIREMENT when HTML has been obtained directly from a Section rule or any other source that does not explicitly define styles. )
3. Add PDF formatting parameters to the current parameter page.
4. Call this activity, making sure to pass the current parameter page to it, as the document will be placed onto the parameter page.
5. Consume the "PDFDocument" parameter, which is of java type byte[] (byte array), and contains the PDF document: * The bytes of the PDF can be used as the first parameter when calling "tools.sendFile" to send the PDF to the client's browser.
* The PDF can be saved to the server using a File Connector
* The PDF can be stored in the database in a Rule-File-eForm record or Rule-File-Binary record.
pagedata.pyLabelOld: Activity to convert HTML stream to PDF .
pagedata.pyDescription:
ACTIVITY TO CONVERT HTML TO PDF .THE INPUT CAN BE A MARKUP OR HTMLSTREAM WHICH IS USED FOR PDF GENERATION. RETURNS THE PDF BYTES.
PLEASE NOTE: * WHEN USING THIS ACTIVITY TO PRODUCE A PDF VERSION OF INFORMATION THAT IS DISPLAYED IN PRPC, MAKE SURE THAT THE HTML IS BEING OBTAINED IN A WAY SUCH THAT THE HEAD ELEMENT INCLUDES THE STYLES FROM THE CORRECT SKIN.
*SIMPLY PIPING THE HTML STREAM OF A SECTION RULE TO THIS ACTIVITY WILL NOT HAVE THE DESIRED EFFECT.
* THE "PREVIEW" ACTION OF SECTION RULES APPLIES STYLES THAT ARE NOT ACTUALLY REFERENCED IN THE HTML SOURCE OF THE SECTION. A PDF PRODUCED FROM THE SOURCE OF A SECTION WILL NOT MATCH THE PREVIEW!

rowdata.pxWarningMessage: Writing application logic using the Java activity method impacts maintainability, discourages reusability, and increases risk during upgrades. Use this method only when necessary. If executing Java code is required, consider using the Call-Function activity method to execute a Function rule. Using Function rules encourages creating well-defined input and output parameters and can be reused across many different types of rules.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
